title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement: Find the maximum profit you can achieve by buying on one day and selling on a different day.

mistakes.hint1: Think about evaluating two elements: the lowest price seen so far and the current price.
mistakes.hint2: Use two variables to keep track: one for the minimum price and one for the maximum profit.
mistakes.hint3: If you simply update the minimum price when you see a lower one, and calculate profit for the rest, you'll arrive at the solution.
mistakes.hint4: Avoid nested loops (O(n^2)), just do a single pass tracking `min_price`.

mistakes.hint1: What value did you initialize your minimum price to?
mistakes.hint2: It needs to start very high so any actual price in the array will be lower.
mistakes.hint3: If you start `min_price` at 0, it will never update because real prices are > 0.
mistakes.hint4: Set `min_price` to `INT_MAX` or the very first element of the array.

mistakes.hint1: Check the bounds of your loop.
mistakes.hint2: Make sure it doesn't run past the end of the prices array.

mistakes.hint1: If there is only 1 day of prices, you can't buy and sell.
mistakes.hint2: Does your code handle arrays of size 0 or 1 safely?
mistakes.hint3: Check if your logic crashes when trying to access `prices[1]`.

mistakes.hint2: Profit should be (current price) - (minimum price seen so far).
mistakes.hint4: Update max profit with `max(max_profit, current_price - min_price)`.

mistakes.hint1: You have to buy BEFORE you can sell.
mistakes.hint2: Are you calculating profit using a maximum price that occurred *before* the minimum price?
mistakes.hint3: Finding the global max and global min independently doesn't work if the max comes first.
mistakes.hint4: Update the `min_price` as you iterate, and calculate profit strictly based on history.

mistakes.hint1: Is your max profit resetting unexpectedly?
mistakes.hint2: Check if you declared your `max_profit` variable INSIDE the loop.
mistakes.hint3: Variables declared inside a loop are destroyed and recreated on every iteration.
mistakes.hint4: Move `int max_profit = 0;` to the top of your function, outside the `for` loop.

mistakes.hint1: What if the stock market crashes and prices only go down?
mistakes.hint2: If prices are [5, 4, 3, 2, 1], your maximum profit should be 0.
mistakes.hint3: Does your code output a negative profit? You should choose not to buy at all.
mistakes.hint4: Initialize max profit to 0, not a negative number or INT_MIN.
